verification_against_live_controller_sem.claim: decision['state_ref'] == request['state_ref'] always holds for genuine controller output, so replay_state_ref_mismatch can only fire on tampered traces, never false-positive.
verification_against_live_controller_sem.evidence: make_envelope(source,...) sets envelope['state_ref']=deepcopy(source['state_ref']); _response_source(payload,session) only swaps in session.effective_budget and otherwise copies payload (the inbound request) verbatim, so a decision's top-level state_ref is always the deep-copy of its eliciting request's state_ref. Confirmed via positive test at L319 using a real GoalController().handle_request() round-trip, and the negative test at L339 only triggers the error after independently tampering state_ref post-construction.

verification_against_live_controller_sem.claim: Position-maps correctly encode request-before-decision-before-result causality matching real append order.
verification_against_live_controller_sem.evidence: _append_replay_locked(session, request, record) appends [request_row, decision_row] together for decisions (request always gets the lower index), and appends only [result_payload] for results, with issued_actions only populated during decision commit (so a result referencing an action can never be accepted before its decision commits). Since sequence/delivery_index already enforced to increase by exactly 1 per row, list index == trace position, so the >/< comparisons on request_positions/decision_positions/index are the correct causal-order check.

verification_against_live_controller_sem.claim: consumed_action_ids correctly mirrors _commit_result's real dedup: at most one *accepted* 'result'-message_type row per action_id can ever exist in a genuine replay trace, regardless of status (APPLIED or any of REJECTED/STALE/DUPLICATE/CANCELLED/ERROR).
verification_against_live_controller_sem.evidence: _commit_result only calls _append_replay_locked on the terminal ACCEPTED path (L1424ish). Any resubmission for an already-accepted action_id either returns an ack(DUPLICATE) without being appended (byte-identical resubmission) or raises ProtocolError('conflicting_duplicate') with nothing appended (divergent resubmission) — L1352-1359. So two 'result' rows for the same action_id in a replay trace is impossible from the live controller; the new check (status-agnostic, keyed purely on action_id, evaluated before the status-specific transition checks) correctly generalizes beyond the APPLIED-only test fixture to this full non-APPLIED-status space.

verification_against_live_controller_sem.claim: action_bindings.setdefault(...) correctly mirrors issued_actions.setdefault(...) first-claim-wins semantics, including the legitimate shared-action_id-across-decisions scenario (plan-cache reuse on repeated/observation requests with an unchanged PlanningContext digest).
verification_against_live_controller_sem.evidence: _plan() returns the cached session.plan object verbatim when context.digest is unchanged (L1450-1452), so two decisions under different request_ids can legitimately carry the identical uuid4 action_id string. The live controller's issued_actions.setdefault() then binds that action_id to the FIRST request_id only (ActionBinding built from the REQUEST payload's own state_ref/session_epoch, which by the state_ref invariant above equals that decision's own state_ref). The new replay check reproduces this exactly: action_bindings is built by iterating decisions.items() in trace order (dict comprehension over decision_records, which preserves envelope order) with .setdefault(), so the first decision in the trace wins the binding; a result attempted under the second (non-owning) request_id is rejected as replay_result_binding_mismatch, matching _commit_result's own binding.request_id != payload['request_id'] rejection (L1320-1324) for the identical scenario — the live controller never persists that rejected attempt as a 'result' row either, so this is a tamper-only rejection, not a false positive on real output.

verification_against_live_controller_sem.claim: Test test_replay_mirrors_first_action_binding_across_shared_decisions genuinely exercises reachable controller behavior, not a fabricated impossible scenario.
verification_against_live_controller_sem.evidence: Traced the mechanism producing the shared action_id end-to-end: source_b is built via observation_request (event_kind='observation'), which reuses session.last_interpretation verbatim (handle_request L1238-1240) rather than re-interpreting, so its typed_intent/intent_id are byte-identical to decision_a's; combined with identical state_ref and observation, PlanningContext.build's digest (hash of {state_ref, observation, typed_intent, intent_id}) is necessarily identical for both decisions, which is exactly what makes _plan()'s cache-hit condition (session.context_digest == context.digest) true for decision_b — hence identical action_id. This is an existing, legitimate controller code path (observation-driven replan short-circuit), not something invented for the test.

prior_checks_preserved.confirmed_by: git diff showing only two '-' lines in the whole npc_goal.py hunk: (1) 'for payload in envelopes:' -> enumerate() wrapper, purely mechanical, same iteration order/members; (2) decision['state_ref'] -> binding[2] in the _result_transition_error call, proven value-identical to decision['state_ref'] at that call site because by that point binding[0]==payload['request_id'] has already been enforced, making 'decision' (looked up by payload['request_id']) the same object that owns the binding. No content-hash, identity, sequence, state_ref-shape, plan-semantics, or transition-error check was removed, loosened, or reordered relative to any check it previously gated.
prior_checks_preserved.test_side: 15/15 pre-existing test_* methods (hash/revision/plan/transition/claim-verification coverage) present unchanged by name; diff is purely additive on the test file aside from cosmetic ruff line-wrap/whitespace reflow (verified twice across two reformat passes, zero logic delta each time).

residual_static_observations_non_blockin: 'ack' message_type envelopes are accepted by validate()'s top-level enum check but are never inspected by any of the request/decision/result loops (all three explicitly skip non-matching message_type). This is a pre-existing characteristic of ReplayValidator untouched by this diff, and is not reachable from genuine controller output (the live controller never persists ack-only responses into replay_records via _append_replay_locked — only request/decision/accepted-result rows are ever written). Flagged for completeness per the 'seek any remaining straightforward causality/duplicate acceptance' instruction; it is not a counterexample against this diff's correctness and is out of this diff's scope.
Test method name 'test_replay_rejects_resigned_decision_state_ref_mismatch' (L339) is likely a typo for 'reassigned' — cosmetic only, no effect on behavior or assertions.
concrete_counterexamples_found: None. No scenario was found where the new checks reject genuine GoalController-produced replay output, and no scenario was found where a genuine duplicate-consumed-action-result or causality-inverted trace would slip past the new checks.

acceptance_criteria_check.no_avoidable_refactor: Confirmed — both non-additive lines are strictly necessary (enumerate() needed to produce the index consumed by the new position checks; binding[2] needed because _result_transition_error's source_ref must come from the actual binding owner now that ownership is no longer assumed to equal 'the decision matching this result's own request_id').
